tour.title: Package Overview
tour.description: The README introduces tenancy-foundation as the multi-tenancy base for Laravel 13 and Filament v5 apps, with an admin panel and a tenant panel set up by plugins. Tenant users can belong to several tenants. Read it first for the vocabulary used in every later step.

tour.title: Service Provider and Config
tour.description: The service provider is the package entry point. It wires up routes, middleware, events, listeners, observers and policies. The config file holds the switches that make behaviour project-specific, such as how tenants are resolved.
tour.languageLesson: Laravel package service providers register and boot a package's bindings, config and listeners, and are auto-discovered through composer.json.

tour.title: Panels and Plugins
tour.description: AdminPlugin and TenantPlugin configure the two Filament panels: admin on guard admin and tenant on guard web with one subdomain per tenant. The FilamentPanel, AuthGuard and TenantResolution enums are the most depended-on types in the package and define which panel, guard and host strategy is in play.

tour.title: Core Models and Concerns
tour.description: Tenant, User, Admin and the Invitation, Role and ContactRequest models form the domain. Behaviour is composed through traits such as IsTenant, IsTenantUser and HasTenantMemberships, so consuming apps get tenancy by using traits on their own models. TenantUser is the membership link, which is how a user belongs to several tenants.
tour.languageLesson: PHP traits let a package ship reusable model behaviour that an app mixes into its own Eloquent classes.

tour.title: Database Schema
tour.description: The migrations create the tenants table, add tenancy columns to users, and create admin users, invitations, contact requests, domain rules and role permission changes. They give the models from the previous step their persistent shape.

tour.title: Actions for Business Logic
tour.description: Business operations live in single-purpose Action classes rather than controllers or models. CreateTenant, CancelTenant and AddTenantOwner are typical examples, and they run in transactions and dispatch events. Filament resources and listeners call these actions.
tour.languageLesson: The Action pattern puts one business operation in one class with a handle() method, which makes it easy to reuse and test.

tour.title: Events and Listeners
tour.description: Actions announce what happened through events such as TenantCancelled, and listeners react with notifications and cleanup. This keeps side effects like welcome mails out of the actions. The app can override listeners using the stubs the install command publishes.

tour.title: Authorisation and Permissions
tour.description: Role and permission enums define the roles and abilities for the admin and tenant sides. AuthorisationPolicy is the shared base for the policies, and the permission matrix support classes and the ManageRolePermissions page let admins edit what each role may do. Seeders load the defaults.

tour.title: Invitations and Registration
tour.description: Invitations let tenant owners bring users in, and registration pages create a tenant together with its first owner. The invitation actions create, send and accept invitations, and the InvalidInvitation exception guards bad tokens.

tour.title: Filament Admin and Tenant UI
tour.description: The admin panel's resources manage tenants, users, admins and contact requests, while the tenant panel manages its own users and invitations. Shared pieces in Filament/Components, such as table actions, columns and schemas, are reused by both panels.

tour.title: Impersonation, Contact and Guards
tour.description: Admins can impersonate tenant users through a handoff that crosses hosts. The middleware bind sessions to hosts and keep unknown or cancelled tenants out, and guard classes protect rules such as keeping the sole owner. Contact requests flow from a public form through actions and events to admin notifications.
